title: Methods and parameters
hook: A method is a named operation with a signature the compiler overloads on. Ordinary parameters come first: value copy for structs, reference copy for classes. Optional arguments, named arguments, and params collections are how you keep call sites readable in workers and importers.

sections.heading: Signatures and overloading
sections.prose: The compiler distinguishes methods by name plus parameter types (and ref-kind, covered next). Return type is not part of the overload identity. Optional parameters must follow required ones; they bake the default into the caller’s IL, so changing a default is a binary breaking change for already-compiled callers — prefer overloads at public library boundaries. Named arguments document intent at SQS handler entry points where three strings in a row are a review hazard.

sections.heading: Ordinary parameter passing
sections.prose: For a class, the callee receives a copy of the reference and can mutate the object unless the type is designed immutable. For a struct, the callee receives a copy of the data; mutating the parameter does not mutate the caller’s variable. That is why a large mutable struct as a parameter is both a correctness and a performance smell. Pass interfaces and classes when you want shared identity; pass small values when you want snapshots.

snippets.label: Overload, optional, and params collections
snippets.explanation: C# 13 params collections allow params IEnumerable<string>, not only arrays. Collection expressions at the call site stay readable for a CSV import header line.

sections.heading: params collections
sections.prose: Historically params meant a trailing array. Starting with C# 13, params can target other collection types the compiler knows how to populate (including span-backed and interface types such as IEnumerable<T> depending on the target). Callers still write a comma-separated argument list. Use params for log scopes and header lists; do not use it as an excuse to skip a named type when the list has structure (column mappings belong in a DTO, not a params blob).

interviewTakeaways: Overload on parameter types, not return types.
Optional-argument defaults are caller-side constants; changing them does not update old assemblies.
Ordinary parameters copy the reference or the struct; ref/in/out are the next topic.
commonPitfalls: Ambiguous overloads with null and optional parameters.
params object[] that erases useful typing at a public API.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS rest (...args) is a real array at runtime. C# params is a compiler rewrite into a collection argument. JS has no overload resolution.
TS overloads are a type-checker fiction over one implementation. C# overloads are distinct methods in metadata.
